paper.title: Which forecasts do error measures rank first, and how long must the test set be?

definitions.definition: Root mean squared error of a point forecast f over a test set of outcomes y_1..y_n: sqrt(mean((y_t - f)^2)).
Mean absolute error of a point forecast f over a test set: mean(|y_t - f|).

Mean absolute percentage error of a point forecast f over a test set: 100 mean(|y_t - f| / |y_t|), for outcomes of either sign. An outcome equal to zero makes it infinite for every forecast; where a distribution has positive density at zero, the expected MAPE of every forecast is infinite. Both are reported as infinite (Inf), not hidden. On counts it is not computed (decision DC3).
Symmetric mean absolute percentage error of a point forecast f over a test set: 200 mean(|y_t - f| / (|y_t| + |f|)), where a pair with y_t = f (including y_t = f = 0) contributes 0.

A point forecast whose value is fixed before any test set is drawn and is the same for every test set. In this study each candidate is computed from the true outcome distribution (its mean, its median, the value with the lowest expected MAPE, the value with the lowest expected sMAPE, or zero); it is never estimated from a test set or from any other sample.

The value a measure gives a candidate forecast in the limit of an infinitely long test set from the outcome distribution: for RMSE sqrt(E[(Y - f)^2]); for MAE E|Y - f|; for MAPE 100 E[|Y - f| / |Y| given Y != 0]; for sMAPE 200 E[|Y - f| / (|Y| + |f|)]. Computed from the distribution itself (by numerical integration, or exact sums for counts), not from simulated test sets.
Of the candidate forecasts for one outcome distribution, the one with the lowest expected score under a given measure. It says which candidate the measure rewards, independently of any test set.

For one outcome distribution, one measure and one test-set size n: for each candidate forecast, the share of simulated test sets of n outcomes in which the measure gives that candidate the lowest score among all candidates (a tie between k candidates gives each 1/k). Its distribution over the candidates, and that distribution's mean, show where a test set of n outcomes puts the measure's choice. It is a count over test sets of a choice among fixed forecasts; it is not a test, and it is not about the value of the measure itself nor about any forecast estimated from data.

Outcomes from a normal distribution with mean 100 and standard deviation 1, 5, 10 or 15, and from a Laplace distribution with location 100 and standard deviation 1, 2.5, 5 or 7.5 (scale sd / sqrt(2)): coefficients of variation from 1% to 15%. Mean and median are both 100. The Laplace stops at 7.5 because its exponential tail puts a share 0.5 exp(-sqrt(2) / CV) of outcomes at or below zero (about 3 in a billion at CV 0.075); outcomes at or below zero are counted as a diagnostic.

Outcomes y = 100 exp(x): lognormal (x normal with mean 0 and standard deviation s, s = 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1) and log-Laplace (x Laplace with location 0 and scale b, b = 0.25, 0.5); and gamma outcomes with mean 100 and shape 2, 5 or 20. All are positive with a density that vanishes at zero, so the expected MAPE is finite.
Symmetric outliers: 95% of outcomes from N(100, 5^2) and 5% from N(100, 15^2). Upward spikes: outcomes from N(100, 5^2), of which 5% are multiplied by 3, as from promotions.
Counts of which more than half are zero: negative binomial with size 1 and mean 0.3, 0.5 or 0.6, and Poisson with mean 0.3, 0.5 or 0.65. MAPE is not computed on counts.

For each outcome distribution, the candidate forecasts are fixed first, and their expected scores computed (continuous distributions: from one reference sample of 10,000,000 outcomes drawn once with its own seed; counts: exactly, from the probability mass function). Then, for each test-set size n = 10, 30, 50, 100, 500, 1,000 and 100,000, test sets of n outcomes are drawn (1,000 for each size under 100,000, 200 at 100,000); in each, every candidate is scored by every measure, and the candidate with the lowest score is counted as that measure's choice (a tie between k candidates counts 1/k for each). No forecast is estimated from a test set.

Outcomes from an inverse Gaussian distribution with mean 100 and shape 1000, 200, 100, 50, 20 or 10 (coefficient of variation sqrt(100 / shape): 0.32 to 3.16): positive, with long right tails, so that ln y is skewed to the right.

Outcomes y = 100 exp(X), X = s * sd * (G - k) / sqrt(k), G from a gamma distribution with shape k = 1, 4 or 16 and scale 1, s = +1 or -1, sd = 0.5 or 1: ln y has standard deviation sd and skewness s * 2 / sqrt(k) (+-2, +-1, +-0.5); with the symmetric case, lognormal with the same sd. Positive, with the skewness of ln y controlled in both directions.

Outcomes y = 100 exp(X), X from N(-1, 0.25^2) with probability p and N(+1, 0.25^2) otherwise: two modes, at about 37 and 272. p = 0.5 (equally high modes), 0.65 (the left one higher), 0.35 (the right one higher).
Outcomes from a normal distribution with standard deviation 1 and mean 0, 0.5 or 1: 50%, 31% and 16% of them negative. The expected MAPE of every forecast is infinite on them.

evidence.description: Lab runs RN1 under plan PL4. Design: The selection design over 28 outcome distributions: symmetric positive (normal with standard deviation 1, 5, 10, 15 and Laplace with standard deviation 1, 2.5, 5, 7.5, at level 100), skewed positive (lognormal s = 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1; log-Laplace b = 0.25, 0.5; gamma shape 2, 5, 20), with outliers (symmetric outliers; upward spikes), counts (Poisson 1.5, 3.5, 10) and intermittent counts (negative binomial mean 0.3, 0.5, 0.6; Poisson 0.3, 0.5, 0.65). Candidates for each: the quantiles at levels 0.01 to 0.99, the mean, and the minimisers of the expected MAPE (continuous only) and sMAPE, merged where equal; continuous distributions from one reference sample of 10,000,000 outcomes (seed 1001 with the setting's index), counts exactly. Test sets of n = 6, 8, 12, 13, 14, 18, 24, 36, 48 (holdout lengths of single series: the M4 competition's 6, 8, 13, 14, 18 and 48, and 12, 24 and 36), 100, 250, 500, 1,000 and 10,000 (errors pooled across series) outcomes, 1,000 test sets per size (seed 1 with the setting's index and n). Measures: RMSE, MAE, MAPE (continuous only) and sMAPE. claimset-code/measure-rankings/simulate.py --seed 1 --ref-seed 1001 --reps-small 1000 (numpy 2.5.3, matplotlib 3.11.2). Analysis: Per distribution and measure: the preferred candidate (lowest expected score), its value and its quantile level. Per distribution, measure and n, over the test sets, of the candidate ranked first (its quantile level for continuous distributions, its value for counts; a tie between k candidates counts 1/k each): the share of test sets choosing each candidate; the 5th, 25th, 50th, 75th and 95th percentiles; the mean with its 99% confidence interval (mean +/- 2.576 standard errors); and the share of test sets choosing the preferred candidate, with its 99% Wilson interval. Figures: per distribution and measure, one violin per n of the choices, a boxplot inside (median, quartiles, 5th and 95th percentiles) with the mean of the choices marked beside it, and every measure's preferred candidate as a labelled line; a candidate that is not a quantile (the mean, a minimiser) is placed at its own quantile level, the share of the distribution at or below it. These are estimates; no test is made and no threshold is set.
